answer: Proof-of-retrievable-storage resists sybils: each identity must commit a large block of identity-salted data and, on randomly-timed audits from dawn onward, return challenged fragments that only the real stored copy can produce. Because the data is salted per identity, one onyx-black disk cannot be shared across a garden of fakes — K identities need K times the committed storage simultaneously, not a deduplicated single copy. An honest agent keeps one dataset cheaply; a swarm hits a hard per-head disk cost, so fleets are capped by physical storage, not by compute that parallelizes.
